en: The Hymn of Earnest Attention (or the Hymn of Veneration): Om, homage to the Lord of the World! You have been propitiated by the hosts of the worlds of nāgas and asuras, and you are praised by gandharvas, yakṣas, and sages.
I perpetually bow my head in homage to the one who consists of compassion, adorned with the thirty-two primary marks of excellence. || 1 ||

I perpetually bow my head in homage to the one whose body possesses a splendor equal to ten million rising suns, who is gazed upon while being borne upon the crest of the Sugatas, who is marked by the moon as a tilaka upon his crown, who wears matted locks, and who is composed of compassion. (2)

I perpetually bow my head to the one whose nature is compassion, who is seated upon a lotus with a lotus in hand, beautifully adorned by a sacred thread and the king of serpents, and resplendent with ornaments of gold and necklaces of jewels. || 3 ||

I bow my head forever to the one whose nature is compassion, who enables crossing the ocean of existence with its arising and ceasing, who liberates from the difficult-to-grasp realms of miserable rebirth, and who is perfectly pure, being utterly free from the defects of passion and the like. 4.

I bow my head in eternal homage to the one whose nature is compassion, who nourishes all sentient beings with the streams of nectar through the four divine abodes beginning with loving-kindness, and who shatters the defects created by the darkness of delusion.

I perpetually bow my head to the one who is composed of compassion, who grants liberation from the forest infested by the lineage of the lords of the Daityas, who has made a firm resolve to swiftly benefit sentient beings, and whose teaching is filled with the knowledge of the Omniscient One.

I perpetually bow my head in homage to the one whose essence is compassion, who purifies the path of the eighteen hells, who utterly dispels the dense darkness of ignorance, and who bestows liberation by gazing with the singular vision of primordial wisdom. 7.

O Lord of the World, Sovereign of the Universe, most generous one, for the sake of shattering the cage of the suffering of poverty, I perpetually bow my head in homage to you, who are filled with compassion and whose pair of lotus feet are worshipped by all. 8.

I bow to you, who possess the splendor of the orb of the sun, whose nature is suchness (*tathatā*), and who bestow excellent fruits through your stainless power; I, though eternally unfortunate, bow my head to you, who are like a wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*) and consist of compassion. (9)

O Compassionate One, lift me up from this ocean of suffering—I who, out of devotion, have bowed my head with the palms of ten fingers joined in the highest form of salutation at Your lotus feet with the eight limbs; I perpetually prostrate with my head before You, the embodiment of mercy. 10.

On the seventh or eighth lunar day of the bright fortnight, when the moon is in the asterisms of Tārā, Punarvasu, or Sahā, on a Friday, and on the day of the Śrī-Krauñcadāraṇa festival, I offer this hymn of praise; O sole Lord of the world, grant me my desired fruit.
Those who recite this great merit, which is purifying and destructive of evil, shall attain the fulfillment of all desires and purposes and go to Sukhāvatī. || 12 ||
The hymn of praise to the venerable Lord Śrīmad Āryāvalokiteśvara, entitled "The Hymn of Attentive Devotion," is completed.
